mastery_goal.title: Coordinate-Plane Graphs
mastery_goal.exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.family_purpose: Directly show that a student can locate an ordered pair on a coordinate plane.
families.evidence_job: plot a point from an ordered pair
families.student_action: Plot the given ordered pair on a coordinate plane.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given ordered pair -> produced graph point

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Plot and read ordered pairs.
variation_axes: change the ordered pair across quadrants
include points on an axis when appropriate
vary which coordinate is zero or negative
forbidden_variations: changing only the point name
using a non-coordinate representation as the only evidence
families.best_use: Best for clean evidence of coordinate plotting.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid when the target is graph scale rather than ordered-pair location.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Plot a Given Ordered Pair evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
Plot the point \(P(-4,3)\) on the coordinate plane.

Place and label point P.
exemplar.solution: Move 4 units left from the origin and 3 units up; place P there.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 1 point: point is plotted at (-4,3) and identified as P.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.family_name: Translate Movement to an Ordered Pair
families.family_purpose: Use directional movement from the origin as an alternate route into coordinate meaning.
families.student_action: Convert verbal horizontal/vertical movement into an ordered pair.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given spatial movement -> produced ordered pair

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Plot and read ordered pairs.
variation_axes: vary directions and distances
include an axis endpoint
reverse the order of the movement statements
forbidden_variations: merely changing the numbers in an ordered-pair plotting prompt
asking for slope or distance
families.best_use: Useful for connecting ordered-pair notation to movement on axes.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid when a visual graph must be the evidence source.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Translate Movement to an Ordered Pair evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
Start at the origin. Move 6 units right and 2 units down. Write the ordered pair for the ending point.

Ordered pair: __________
exemplar.solution: Right gives a positive x-coordinate, 6. Down gives a negative y-coordinate, -2.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.family_purpose: Reveal whether the student understands how direction determines coordinate signs.
families.student_action: Identify the specific coordinate-sign error and give the correct ordered pair.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given worked claim -> produced diagnosis + correction

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Plot and read ordered pairs.
variation_axes: vary the mistaken sign or coordinate
use quadrants II, III, or IV
occasionally include a correct claim that must be defended
forbidden_variations: generic “find the mistake” without a specific worked claim
changing only the point name
families.best_use: Strong misconception check for coordinate signs.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid for first exposure before students know axis directions.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Diagnose a Coordinate Sign Error evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
A student says, “From the origin I moved 3 units left and 5 units up, so the point is \( (3,5) \).” Explain the error and write the correct ordered pair.

Explain and correct:
exemplar.answer: The x-coordinate should be -3, so the point is (-3, 5).
exemplar.solution: Moving left makes the x-coordinate negative; moving up makes the y-coordinate positive.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 2 points: 1 for identifying the x-sign error; 1 for (-3,5).

i_cans.exact_text: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
families.family_purpose: Directly test which coordinate controls horizontal versus vertical movement.
families.evidence_job: use x first and y second correctly
families.student_action: Follow x- then y-coordinate movement to locate a point.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation
families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
variation_axes: vary quadrant and zero coordinates
ask axis role before plotting
switch between words horizontal/vertical and x/y
forbidden_variations: testing only sign knowledge
changing labels without changing the axis decision
families.best_use: Best direct evidence of x/y axis roles.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid when scale reading is the main target.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Axis-First Coordinate Move evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
For the point \(Q(2,-6)\), which axis tells you to move 2 units, and which axis tells you to move -6 units? Then plot Q.

Name the axes and place Q.
exemplar.answer: x-axis: 2 units right; y-axis: 6 units down; Q=(2,-6).
exemplar.solution: The first coordinate is x and controls horizontal movement; the second is y and controls vertical movement.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 2 points: 1 for correct axis roles; 1 for correct plot.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
families.family_purpose: Apply axis conventions in a simple relationship context.
families.evidence_job: choose appropriate x and y axis roles from a context
families.student_action: Assign input/independent and output/dependent quantities to graph axes.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation
families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
variation_axes: vary common input/output contexts
provide unlabeled axes for students to label
ask whether a proposed axis assignment is sensible
forbidden_variations: using a context where axis roles are genuinely ambiguous
turning the item into slope interpretation
families.best_use: Good alternate evidence for axis meaning beyond pure coordinate notation.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid with contexts that do not imply a clear input/output order.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Assign Variables to Axes evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
A graph will show distance traveled as time passes.

Which quantity belongs on the x-axis, and which belongs on the y-axis? Explain in one sentence.

Axis assignment + reason:
exemplar.answer: Time on the x-axis; distance on the y-axis.
exemplar.solution: Time is the input that progresses, and distance is measured for each time value.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 2 points: 1 for correct axes; 1 for a sensible input/output explanation.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
families.family_purpose: Target the common mistake of reversing x and y movement.
families.evidence_job: diagnose reversal of x- and y-axis roles
families.student_action: Explain why a plotted location does not match the ordered pair.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given incorrect axis procedure -> produced diagnosis

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
variation_axes: vary signs and quadrants
vary whether the error is swapping axes or swapping signs
sometimes ask students to describe the resulting wrong point
forbidden_variations: vague error prompts with no stated procedure
errors unrelated to axis roles
families.best_use: Efficient misconception evidence on coordinate order.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid when students have not yet learned ordered-pair conventions.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Diagnose an Axis Swap evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
To plot \(R(-2,7)\), Maya moves 7 units left and 2 units up. What did Maya reverse? State the correct movements.

Diagnosis:
exemplar.answer: She reversed the coordinates. Move 2 units left, then 7 units up.
exemplar.solution: The first coordinate, -2, controls horizontal x movement; the second, 7, controls vertical y movement.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 2 points: 1 for naming the reversal; 1 for correct movements.

i_cans.exact_text: Read a graph using its scale.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Read a graph using its scale.
families.family_purpose: Read a value from a graph whose tick spacing must be interpreted.
families.evidence_job: read a graph value using its displayed scale
families.student_action: Determine a y-value at a specified x-value from a scaled graph.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation
families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Read a graph using its scale.
variation_axes: vary axis intervals
use x or y lookup
include decimal or larger-unit scales when appropriate
forbidden_variations: unit-scale-only graphs
questions answerable without reading the scale
families.avoid_uses: Avoid when the graph is decorative rather than necessary.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Read a Scaled Coordinate evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
Use the graph. At \(t=4\) minutes, what distance is shown?

Distance: __________ m
exemplar.solution: The line is at 70 when t=4, using the y-axis scale rather than counting gridlines as ones.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Read a graph using its scale.
families.family_name: Compare Values on an Unequal Scale
families.family_purpose: Require scale reading at two positions and a comparison, not a single lookup.
families.evidence_job: use graph scale to compare two represented values
families.student_action: Read two graph values and compute their difference.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given scaled graph -> two readings -> produced difference

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Read a graph using its scale.
variation_axes: vary the two lookup positions
compare additive or multiplicative change when natural
vary labeled intervals
forbidden_variations: making the second step independent of the graph readings
using identical scale and values every time
families.best_use: Good application when one lookup would be too shallow.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid if the arithmetic obscures the scale-reading target.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Compare Values on an Unequal Scale evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
Use the graph. How much more water is shown at 8 minutes than at 3 minutes?

Show the two readings and the difference.
exemplar.solution: The graph shows 200 L at 8 min and 100 L at 3 min. The difference is 100 L.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 3 points: 1 for each correct graph reading; 1 for 100 L difference.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Read a graph using its scale.
families.family_purpose: Expose whether students infer value from labels instead of assuming unit spacing.
families.student_action: Correct a value obtained by counting gridlines as units.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given scaled graph + incorrect reading -> produced diagnosis

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Read a graph using its scale.
variation_axes: vary assumed grid value
use x-axis or y-axis misconception
vary graph scale
forbidden_variations: error statements that do not depend on the scale
asking only for the correct number with no diagnosis
families.best_use: High-value check for the documented unit-scale assumption.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid on a graph where every gridline actually is 1.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Diagnose “Each Gridline Is 1” evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
A student uses this graph and says the value at 4 minutes is 4 because the point is four grid spaces above 0.

Explain why that reading is wrong and give the correct value.

Explain:
exemplar.answer: 70 m; the grid spacing represents more than 1 unit.
exemplar.solution: Axis labels determine what each grid interval means. Reading the y-scale at t=4 gives 70 m.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 2 points: 1 for scale explanation; 1 for 70 m.

i_cans.exact_text: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.
families.family_purpose: Directly identify x- and y-intercepts from a graph.
families.evidence_job: identify x- and y-intercepts from a displayed graph
families.student_action: Read and name both intercept coordinates.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation
families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.
variation_axes: vary line direction and intercept signs
ask for one or both intercepts
include intercept at the origin only when interpretation remains clear
forbidden_variations: asking for slope instead of intercepts
graphs with intercepts hidden outside the window
families.avoid_uses: Avoid if the graph does not visibly show the intercept.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Identify Both Intercepts evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
Identify the x-intercept and y-intercept of the line.

x-intercept: ______   y-intercept: ______
exemplar.solution: An x-intercept has y=0; a y-intercept has x=0.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.
families.family_purpose: Use a contextual graph to assign meaning to an intercept.
families.evidence_job: interpret what an intercept means for two related quantities
families.student_action: State the meaning and units of a displayed intercept.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given contextual graph -> produced verbal interpretation

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.
variation_axes: vary initial-value contexts
switch between x- and y-intercept when meaningful
require units
forbidden_variations: contexts where an intercept has no sensible meaning
asking only for coordinate identification
families.avoid_uses: Avoid artificial contexts with meaningless zero input.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Interpret an Intercept in Context evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
The graph shows a service cost over time.

What does the y-intercept mean in this situation?

Interpretation:
exemplar.answer: The cost is $20 at 0 hours; $20 is the starting fee.
exemplar.solution: The y-intercept occurs when x=0, so it represents the initial cost before any hourly time is added.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 2 points: 1 for $20 at 0 hours; 1 for contextual meaning as starting fee.

families.mastery_goal_exact_text: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
families.i_can_exact_text: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.
families.family_purpose: Diagnose the common confusion between which coordinate is zero.
families.student_action: Explain whether a stated intercept name matches its coordinate.
families.representation_need: required when it carries evidence; otherwise no decorative representation

representation_routes.type: given graph + intercept claim -> produced diagnosis

families.invariant: Student evidence must directly demonstrate: Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.
variation_axes: vary which intercept is mislabeled
use negative intercepts
ask for a rule that distinguishes intercepts
forbidden_variations: errors about slope rather than intercept identity
graphs that do not show both needed intercepts
families.best_use: Strong reasoning check for intercept definitions.
families.avoid_uses: Avoid before students can identify axes reliably.
families.fresh_instance_rule: Create a new instance that preserves the Distinguish x- from y-Intercept evidence architecture, changes at least two meaningful parameters/representation features when possible, and remains equivalent in mastery demand without copying the exemplar surface.

exemplar.student_html:
A student looks at the line and says, “\((0,6)\) is the x-intercept because it is on an axis.”

Correct the statement and explain how you know.

Correction:
exemplar.answer: (0,6) is the y-intercept; the x-intercept is (3,0).
exemplar.solution: A y-intercept has x=0 and lies on the y-axis. An x-intercept has y=0 and lies on the x-axis.
exemplar.scoring_guidance: 3 points: correct name, correct other intercept, correct zero-coordinate explanation.
